theory.intro: Describe skewness from the tail of a distribution: a tail to the right is positively skewed and a tail to the left is negatively skewed. The mean uses every value and can be distorted by outliers; the median uses the middle position or positions, and the mode identifies the most frequent value.
facts: **Positively skewed** means the distribution has a longer tail to the right. For a typical single-peaked shape like the booklet's illustration, the measures often follow $\text{mode} < \text{median} < \text{mean}$. This is a tendency, not a rule for every dataset.

**Negatively skewed** means the distribution has a longer tail to the left. For a typical single-peaked shape like the booklet's illustration, the measures often follow $\text{mean} < \text{median} < \text{mode}$. This is a tendency, not a rule for every dataset.

**Symmetrical** distributions have matching shapes on either side of their centre. Their mean and median are equal when defined. A symmetrical bell-shaped distribution has a central mode, but symmetrical distributions can also be bimodal or multimodal.
A very large or very small value can change the mean substantially. The median is less affected by the size of an outlier, although changing the dataset can change its middle positions.
On a smooth distribution curve, mark the mode or modes below the peaks. A grouped histogram identifies a modal class rather than an exact modal value.
The mean, median and mode alone do not determine the shape of a distribution. Describe the shape from the data display rather than using their ordering as a reverse test.
A uniform distribution has equally frequent values. Following the booklet's convention, it has **no mode**. For equally spaced values with equal frequencies, the mean and median are equal.
Choose a measure of centre that represents the data and the purpose. A mean distorted by an outlier or a mode far from most values can be misleading.
steps: Read the data or distribution display
Describe the tail and peaks, or calculate the requested measures
Use the display and context to explain your answer

workedExamples.solution_text:
A is positively skewed: its longer tail extends to the right.

B is negatively skewed: its longer tail extends to the left.

C is symmetrical: its two sides mirror each other about the central peak.
The columns become shorter towards the right, forming a longer right-hand tail. The distribution is positively skewed.

workedExamples.question_text:
A student's eight test scores were $9,6,9,6,9,5,9,4$.

Find the mean, median and mode. Which measure would the student prefer to report to make their performance appear best?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Order the scores: $4,5,6,6,9,9,9,9$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Mean}&=\frac{4+5+6+6+9+9+9+9}{8}\\&=\frac{57}{8}\\&=7.125\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Median}&=\frac{6+9}{2}\\&=7.5\end{aligned}$

The mode is $9$, occurring four times. The student would prefer to report the mode because it is the highest of the three measures.

workedExamples.question_text: For the scores $4,5,5,5,7,7,7,7,7$, find the mode, median and mean. Explain why the mode and median are less useful measures of centre here.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The mode is $7$, occurring five times. There are nine ordered scores, so the median is the fifth score, also $7$.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Mean}&=\frac{4+5+5+5+7+7+7+7+7}{9}\\&=\frac{54}{9}\\&=6\end{aligned}$

The mode and median both equal the largest score, so neither represents a value between the lower and upper scores. The mean, $6$, lies between the two groups.

workedExamples.question_text:
Consider Dataset A: $14,14,15,16,17$ and Dataset B: $14,14,15,16,117$.

Calculate each mean and explain why the mean represents Dataset A better. Would the median or mode better represent the centre of Dataset B?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Mean of A}&=\frac{76}{5}\\&=15.2\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Mean of B}&=\frac{176}{5}\\&=35.2\end{aligned}$

Dataset A's mean lies near its values. In Dataset B, the outlier $117$ pulls the mean far above the other four values.

Dataset B's median is $15$ and its mode is $14$. The median better represents the middle of the ordinary values; the mode is their lowest value.

workedExamples.question_text:
Ten trains had delays of $0,0,0,0,0,1,2,3,6,38$ minutes.

Find the mean, median and mode. Explain which measure passengers might use to emphasise substantial delays and which measure the operator might use to present the service favourably.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Mean}&=\frac{50}{10}\\&=5\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Median}&=\frac{0+1}{2}\\&=0.5\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$

The mode is $0$ minutes.

Passengers might use the mean because it includes the severe delay of $38$ minutes. The operator might use the mode to emphasise that arriving on time is the most frequent result. The mode leaves out the size of the longer delays.

workedExamples.question_text: A shoe store sold sizes $5,6,6,7,7,7,8,8,9,10$. Which measure of centre would help the owner decide which size to stock more of? Explain.
workedExamples.solution_text: The mode is size $7$, occurring three times. It identifies the most frequently sold size, so it helps the owner decide which size to stock more of.

workedExamples.question_text:
Seven employees earn $\$36{,}000$ each and one employee earns $\$436{,}000$. An advertisement reports a mean salary of $\$86{,}000$.

Check the mean and explain why it gives a misleading impression of a typical salary.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Mean salary}&=\frac{7\times36{,}000+436{,}000}{8}\\&=\frac{688{,}000}{8}\\&=86{,}000\end{aligned}$

The mean is correctly reported as $\$86{,}000$. However, seven of the eight employees earn $\$36{,}000$. The single high salary pulls the mean upwards. The median, $\$36{,}000$, better represents a typical salary.

workedExamples.question_text:
A student's score categories were:

| Score category | Number of tests |
| --- | --- |
| 20s | 1 |
| 30s | 1 |
| 40s | 1 |
| 50s | 1 |
| 60s | 1 |
| 70s | 3 |
| 80s | 0 |
| 90s | 0 |

The student reports only that the modal category is the 70s. Explain why this can give a misleading impression.
workedExamples.solution_text: The 70s is the modal category because it has the greatest frequency, three tests. However, five of the eight scores are below the 70s. Reporting only the modal category makes the overall performance appear stronger than it is.

workedExamples.question_text:
The plots show scores for two groups. Is Group A generally higher scoring than Group B? Explain using clustering and skewness.

| Group A leaves | Stem | Group B leaves |
| ---: | :---: | :--- |
|  | 1 | 2 4 6 8 |
| 8 | 2 | 2 5 8 |
| 8 5 | 3 | 2 7 |
| 8 6 3 | 4 | 2 |
| 8 6 4 2 | 5 | 4 |
| 4 | 6 |  |

Key: a leaf $8$ beside stem $2$ represents $28$.
workedExamples.solution_text: Yes. Group A clusters in the 40s and 50s, with a tail towards lower scores, so it is negatively skewed. Group B clusters in the teens and 20s, with a tail towards higher scores, so it is positively skewed. Group A's main cluster is higher.

workedExamples.question_text:
Twenty students took a topic test before and after teaching.

| Score | Pre-test frequency | Post-test frequency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 3 | 0 |
| 1 | 7 | 1 |
| 2 | 6 | 3 |
| 3 | 3 | 6 |
| 4 | 1 | 7 |
| 5 | 0 | 3 |

Describe each distribution and explain how the scores changed.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The pre-test distribution is positively skewed: scores cluster towards the lower end, with a tail towards higher scores.

The post-test distribution is negatively skewed: scores cluster towards the higher end, with a tail towards lower scores.

Scores generally improved after teaching.

foundation.question_text: The scores are $1, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4$. Calculate the mode and explain why it is not a good measure of centre.
foundation.solution_text: The mode is $4$, which occurs five times. It is the largest score, so it does not represent the centre of the scores.

foundation.question_text: The scores are $3, 4, 4, 4, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6$. Calculate the median and explain why it is not a good measure of centre.
foundation.solution_text: There are nine ordered scores, so the median is the fifth score, $6$. It is the largest score, so it does not represent the centre of the scores.

foundation.question_text: Consider Dataset 1: $10, 10, 11, 12, 13$ and Dataset 2: $10, 10, 11, 12, 113$. Would the median or mode be a better measure of centre for Dataset 2? Explain.
foundation.solution_text: The median is $11$ and the mode is $10$. The median is the better choice because it represents the middle of the ordinary values without being distorted by the outlier $113$.

foundation.question_text: A student scored $7, 4, 7, 4, 7, 3, 7, 2$ in eight tests. Find the mean, mode and median.
foundation.solution_text: The ordered scores are $2, 3, 4, 4, 7, 7, 7, 7$. The mean is $41 \div 8 = 5.125$. The mode is $7$. The median is $(4 + 7) \div 2 = 5.5$.

foundation.question_text: A student scored $8, 5, 8, 5, 8, 4, 8, 3$ in eight tests. Which measure of centre would the student prefer to tell their parents? Explain.
foundation.solution_text: The mean is $49 \div 8 = 6.125$, the median is $(5 + 8) \div 2 = 6.5$ and the mode is $8$. The student would prefer the mode because it makes their performance appear best.

foundation.question_text: Consider Dataset 1: $12, 12, 13, 14, 15$ and Dataset 2: $12, 12, 13, 14, 115$. Explain why the mean is a good measure of centre for the first dataset but not the second.
foundation.solution_text: Dataset 1 has mean $66 \div 5 = 13.2$, near the centre of its values. Dataset 2 has mean $166 \div 5 = 33.2$. Its outlier $115$ pulls the mean far above the other four values, so the mean does not represent a typical value.

mastery.question_text: Seven employees each earn $\$32{,}000$ and one employee earns $\$432{,}000$. An advertisement says, 'The mean salary is $\$82{,}000$.' Explain why this summary statistic is misleading.
mastery.solution_text: The mean is $(7 \times 32{,}000 + 432{,}000) \div 8 = 82{,}000$, so the calculation is correct. The single salary of $\$432{,}000$ pulls the mean far above what seven of the eight employees earn. The median, $\$32{,}000$, better represents a typical employee's salary.

mastery.question_text: A student's test scores fall into these categories: 30s: one test; 40s: one; 50s: one; 60s: one; 70s: one; 80s: two; 90s: none. The student says, 'My modal score category is the 80s!' Explain why this summary statistic is misleading.
mastery.solution_text: The 80s is the most frequent category, so the statement is correct. However, only two of the seven scores are in the 80s and five are below that category. Reporting only the modal category makes the overall performance appear stronger than it is.

mastery.question_text:
The ordered scores are shown in stem-and-leaf plots.

Group A: $2\mid4$; $3\mid1\ 3$; $4\mid5\ 6\ 8$; $5\mid0\ 2\ 4\ 5$; $6\mid0$.

Group B: $2\mid0\ 2\ 4\ 5$; $3\mid0\ 2\ 4$; $4\mid0\ 5$; $5\mid0$; $6\mid2$.

Key: $2\mid4 = 24$.

Pat claims that Group A generally scored higher than Group B. Is Pat correct? Refer to clustering and skewness.
mastery.solution_text: Yes. Group A clusters in the 40s and 50s, with a tail towards the lower scores, so it is negatively skewed. Group B clusters in the 20s and 30s, with a tail towards the higher scores, so it is positively skewed. Group A's main cluster is higher.

mastery.question_text:
A topic test was taken before and after teaching. The frequencies for scores $0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ were:

Pre-test: $2, 8, 6, 3, 1, 0$.

Post-test: $0, 1, 3, 6, 8, 2$.

Describe each distribution and comment on how the scores changed.
mastery.solution_text: The pre-test distribution is positively skewed: most scores are low and the tail extends towards higher scores. The post-test distribution is negatively skewed: most scores are high and the tail extends towards lower scores. Scores generally improved after teaching.
